intro.title: First Bad Version
intro.body: In this lesson, you will implement an algorithm to find the first bad version in a series of software releases using a binary search approach. You'll learn how to efficiently minimize the number of API calls by halving the search range at each step. The main technologies involved include JavaScript functions, while loops, and conditional logic. This exercise will help you understand the practical application of binary search in debugging and version control scenarios.
intro.usecase: The First Bad Version algorithm is essential for debugging and quality assurance in software development. When a team discovers a bug in their codebase, they need to quickly identify which commit introduced the issue—this is exactly the 'first bad version' problem. Product dashboards for continuous integration systems like Jenkins or GitHub Actions use this pattern to pinpoint faulty releases. Similarly, mobile app stores use it to determine which app version started crashing, allowing developers to roll back to the last stable release while fixing the problem.
